sampling_model.design: Known history-predictable randomization \(p_{bi}(z\mid H_{bi})\) on ordered enrollment positions.
sampling_model.units: The typed unit-level potential-outcome schedule encodes no cross-unit interference, the observation map \(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{bi}=Y_{bi}(Z_{bi})\) encodes consistency, block membership is fixed, and assignment is the experiment's only endogenous randomness.
sampling_model.treatment: The shared control is available in every block, while the focal arm has positive propensity exactly on the proper block window \(W\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every available arm has compatible-history propensity at least \(p_{\min}>0\); structural zeros off the availability set are allowed, and information is averaged under the induced assignment law.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Outcome regressions \(m_{bi}(z)\) are bounded and predictable; validity does not require consistency of these regressions.
sampling_model.procedure_randomization: A schedule-independent Markov kernel may use an auxiliary \(U_{\mathrm{aux}}\sim\operatorname{Unif}(0,1)\) independent of the assignment experiment; coverage and expected length are computed under that same extended law. The concurrent-only subclass observes all assignment and realized propensity metadata but no outcome outside \(W\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The two-stage adding-arm simulations compare all-control and concurrent-only analyses under linear and step trends, and the stage-adjusted analysis is equivalent to concurrent-only analysis while linear adjustment can fail under nonlinear drift.

Equation (3) writes the two-period regression estimator as a concurrent-control mean plus a weighted nonconcurrent trend adjustment, and Section 3.1.2 gives unbiasedness under equal additive arm trends.

Theorem 3 gives the efficient influence function for the concurrent average treatment effect, and Section 6 finds no first-order doubly robust NCC efficiency gain when availability is deterministic in entry time.
Theorem 4 proves design-unbiasedness and a martingale central limit theorem for finite-population AIPW under adaptive randomization with positive propensity for every analyzed treatment.
Theorems 3.1--3.2 optimize honest confidence intervals through convex-class modulus and worst-case bias geometry in a Gaussian regression experiment.
Theorem 1 lower-bounds the expected length of every honest interval by a between-class Gaussian modulus and constructs constant-factor adaptive intervals over convex classes.
The paper selects data-adaptive external-control weights to keep estimated expected bias below a prespecified cap and reports bootstrap Wald inference under model-based assumptions.

Theorem 4 gives the minimax confidence-interval-length rate and an attaining upper construction in a Gaussian RCT-plus-observational model with bounded scalar confounding bias; Theorem 5 gives the adaptive-confidence-interval lower bound and impossibility.

Definitions 2.1--2.3 define a concurrently randomized cohort by a common allocation design, define nonconcurrent controls by membership outside that cohort, and distinguish contemporaneous controls by same-stage enrollment.

The paper compares categorical fixed-effect, mixed-effect, and spline calendar-time adjustments for platform-trial nonconcurrent controls through simulation-based type-I-error and power analysis, finding spline control for sufficiently smooth trends and period fixed effects most robust for arbitrary equal-across-arm trends.

body.tldr: A late platform arm has randomized concurrent controls but only nonrandom temporal comparability with earlier controls. Direct two-stage analyses under linear or step trends and later fixed-effect, mixed-effect, and spline analyses study model-based bias, type-I error, and power; a total-variation budget on fixed control block means instead makes temporal comparability quantitative without specifying a trend model. A cumulative-discrepancy linear program gives exact worst-case borrowing bias, while a finite-dimensional convex program balances that bias against an assignment-law-averaged AIPW martingale envelope using actual history probabilities rather than worst-path propensity floors. Projecting the estimator onto the feasible effect range yields an observed-data interval that is nonempty on every assignment path and uniformly design-honest without a score-range assumption. The theorem-level target is a universal-constant equivalence between this average-design radius and minimax expected length over all schedule-independent observed-data Markov kernels. The open step is an adaptive fuzzy-prior comparison with an observed-law mixture modulus through an explicit sequential likelihood-ratio or deficiency bound. A KKT certificate determines exactly when the NCC AIPW construction improves on its concurrent-only AIPW counterpart; a separate all-kernel concurrent-only benchmark equals the full-data minimax value when drift is vacuous. A fully specified three-block LP has the exact zero-drift value \(0.7M\), certified by an explicit hull-plus-singletons policy and matching analytic dual; no unsupported numerical value is asserted for its positive-drift or concurrent-only variants.

project_justification.gap: LeeWason2020 directly compares all versus concurrent controls in a two-stage adding-arm platform under parametric linear and step trends and reports stage-adjustment equivalence with concurrent-only analysis. BofillRoigEtAl2022 and KrotkaEtAl2025TemporalDrift analyze fixed, mixed, or spline time-trend adjustments through model-based bias, type-I error, and power, MarschnerSchou2024 analyzes randomized-cohort adjustment, and SantacatterinaEtAl2025 gives a superpopulation efficiency analysis of the concurrent estimand. ChenLiZhangYe2025 Theorem 4 gives the minimax confidence-interval-length rate and attaining upper construction for bounded-confounding Gaussian RCT and observational summaries; Theorem 5 gives the adaptive-confidence-interval lower bound and impossibility. The literature lacks a best uniformly honest fixed-schedule randomization interval under a total-variation calendar-drift class, observed-data measurability, and unequal adaptive-history probabilities.
project_justification.niche: Ordered control block means form a low-dimensional convex nuisance class whose exact support function can be coupled to assignment-law-averaged martingale information under a known adaptive platform design. This creates a design-specific borrowing frontier that does not assume a common trend, retains heterogeneous allocation metadata within the focal availability window, and distinguishes the implementable AIPW certificate from the exact concurrent-only all-kernel benchmark.
project_justification.fill: The formal program consists of the cumulative-sum bias dual, an everywhere-nonempty projected AIPW interval, a matching observed-law mixture lower bound over every schedule-independent randomized interval kernel through a sequential likelihood-ratio or deficiency construction, a pointwise AIPW optimizer certificate, exact full-data versus concurrent-only minimax equality at vacuous drift, and a three-block reduction whose zero-drift value has an explicit primal--dual certificate.

body.related_work: LeeWason2020 is a direct two-stage adding-arm platform comparator: its Methods and equations (1)--(3) compare all-control and concurrent-only analyses under linear and step trends and report that stage adjustment is equivalent to concurrent-only analysis while linear adjustment can fail for nonlinear drift. Its parametric trend analysis does not characterize uniform fixed-schedule coverage over a TV class, history-adaptive randomization, or minimax expected length over all observed-data interval kernels. BofillRoigEtAl2022 is the writing exemplar: its Introduction, equation (1), weighted representation in equation (3), and Conclusions move from staggered entry to efficiency and then to failure under temporal heterogeneity. KrotkaEtAl2025TemporalDrift studies categorical fixed effects, mixed effects, and spline adjustment for calendar time and evaluates type-I error and power in simulations; its spline guarantee is tied to sufficiently smooth trends, while its period adjustment is robust to arbitrary trends under an equal-across-arm trend model. Those model-based operating-characteristic results inform the temporal-drift problem but do not imply uniform coverage or minimax expected length over fixed schedules in a total-variation ball under adaptive randomization. MarschnerSchou2024 Definitions 2.1--2.3 define concurrency through a common randomized cohort rather than calendar time and separate concurrent, nonconcurrent, and contemporaneous controls. The calendar-window record \(O^{\mathrm{cc}}\) is therefore not asserted to equal their cohort object: it retains each realized allocation vector so heterogeneous designs within \(W\) are not collapsed. Their cohort-adjusted regression and network analyses do not study a TV drift class, fixed schedules, or minimax randomization intervals. SantacatterinaEtAl2025, Theorems 1 and 3 and Section 6, clarifies the concurrent estimand and shows why deterministic availability alone does not create a first-order robust NCC gain; the TV restriction is additional cross-block information and the interval pays explicitly for it. LiZhao2026, equation (3), Theorems 4--5, and Lemma S8 provide the finite-population predictable-AIPW martingale template. Structural focal-arm propensity zeros create deterministic NCC bias, and the assignment-law average must respect the induced probability of each adaptive branch. ChenLiZhangYe2025, Theorem 4, gives the minimax confidence-interval-length rate and an attaining upper construction when separate Gaussian RCT and observational summaries differ by bounded confounding bias; Theorem 5 gives the adaptive-confidence-interval lower bound and impossibility. Those results inform the bias--information phase change, but their superpopulation two-sample asymptotics do not subsume a fixed potential-outcome schedule, availability zeros, or history-adaptive randomization. ArmstrongKolesar2018, Sections 3.2--3.4 and the proof of Theorem 3.1, supplies the bias--variance optimization template, while CaiLow2004, Theorem 1 and its mixture proof, supplies the all-interval expected-length logic. Their Gaussian likelihood calculations do not cover schedule-dependent sequential assignment laws. SawadaNomuraShinozaki2026 chooses external-control weights under an estimated bias cap, but its estimand, confounding model, bootstrap interval, and guarantee differ from a fixed-population randomization minimax theorem. AronowLopatto2026 and SudijonoDobribanTchetgen2026 provide bounded finite-population minimax benchmarks without staggered availability, TV borrowing, or observed-data interval kernels.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The all-interval lower bound is not treated as established. The correct benchmark averages information under each schedule's induced adaptive assignment law: a branch with probability \(\epsilon\) and propensity \(\delta\) contributes at most on the order of \(\epsilon/\delta\), so a worst-path \(1/\delta\) radius cannot be the minimax expected-length target without additional reachability assumptions. The fuzzy-prior proof obligation is an explicit adaptive sequential likelihood-ratio or Le Cam deficiency construction that remains inside the TV ball almost surely and compares the resulting observed-data mixture laws. The fully specified one-unit three-block LP permits randomized interval actions and has endpoint grid \(\{-2M,-M,0,M,2M\}\). Only its zero-drift optimum is asserted numerically because the core displays both a reproducible hull-plus-singletons policy and a matching analytic dual; positive-drift and concurrent-only values remain unasserted until equally explicit certificates are available. The finite diagnostic does not prove a universal comparison for arbitrary adaptive designs.
body.honest_scope: The typed schedule convention encodes no cross-unit interference and the observation map encodes consistency; neither is duplicated as a load-bearing assumption. Every remaining assumption is genuinely load-bearing for the design, support, boundedness, or drift class. The projected upper interval is nonempty on every observed path, so no fallback tail or strengthened score-range assumption is required. The drift dual, observed-procedure classes, rare-history calculation, vacuous-drift benchmark equality, and finite LP are constructive targets. The zero-drift three-block claim carries its full primal policy and dual feasibility reduction; the adaptive sequential likelihood-ratio or deficiency construction remains an explicit unresolved proof obligation. The universal-constant comparison between the average AIPW radius and the observed-law mixture modulus is the central open mathematical risk. No schedule-dependent interval is admissible: one observed-data Markov kernel must serve every fixed schedule, and its auxiliary randomizer is independent of the assignment experiment. No claim is made that \(\Gamma\) is identifiable from trial data. The KKT certificate compares the NCC and concurrent-only AIPW radii, not the two all-kernel minimax values. The three-block policy demonstrates that marginal randomized coverage of observationally indistinguishable targets does not force their joint coverage. At \(\gamma=0\), equal control block means license full borrowing according to average design information. At \(\gamma=\Gamma_{\mathrm{vac}}\), the drift condition is vacuous and the full-record and concurrent-only all-kernel minimax values agree.
